claim_being_audited: The Actor's claim that the model can be certified now on aggregate-readiness and governance-process grounds despite the unresolved HR benefits enrollment gap.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy threshold for certification.
A weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case.
Product labels such as non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality when the segment is named in customer commitments or legal review is pending.
Material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
General governance guidance can support documentation and monitoring practices, but it cannot substitute for satisfaction of the specific release-policy requirement.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the HR benefits enrollment gap must be disclosed.
Approved risk-acceptance record explicitly covering this named segment gap before launch, if one exists.
Published or approved model-card/disclosure text showing the material limitation was disclosed for the named launch use case.
Evidence that the HR benefits enrollment gap has been remediated and now meets target.
specific_concerns: Admissible evidence shows the HR benefits enrollment segment misses target by 1.5 percentage points and that segment is named in two employer rollout commitments.

The governing policy states a weakness is material when it affects a named launch use case or contractual customer segment; product 'non-core' labeling does not resolve materiality in that circumstance.
The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
No admissible evidence shows the gap was resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required remains open, leaving a required policy predicate unresolved at decision time.
Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one incidents do not cure an unresolved material-disclosure requirement.
unsupported_claims: That certification is defensible now based primarily on aggregate readiness and rehearsal results.
That model-card guidance and general AI risk-management guidance are sufficient support for launch certification despite the unresolved policy-specific disclosure issue.
That residual risk can simply be managed through deployment without evidence of required disclosure closure or approved risk acceptance.
